title: atomic_dec_if_positive in unregister prevents silent FIPS enforcement bypass
description: Why it is right: crypto2dev_unregister_provider() uses atomic_dec_if_positive() rather than atomic_dec() to decrement fips_provider_count. If the count is already 0 (double-unregister or bug), atomic_dec_if_positive() returns -1 without decrementing, and WARN() fires. A plain atomic_dec() would allow the counter to go negative, which would make atomic_read() > 0 return false and silently disable FIPS enforcement for all subsequent lookups — a CMVP audit finding. What a reviewer might incorrectly suggest: 'atomic_dec is simpler and double-unregister cannot happen in practice.' In kernel module code, module_exit bugs are real; the WARN is the right defense and the check costs nothing on the fast path.
